answer: Cross-Epoch Drift Rule. Each identity commits a behavioural fingerprint (action-type mix, timing histogram) per epoch; the rule requires the next-epoch fingerprint to stay within a similarity corridor of the prior one, forming a vine of chained commitments. An identity must also clear a minimum activity ridge each epoch or decay. Sybils that split into many fresh identities hit the corridor nadir immediately, since new identities lack history to match.
